SupplySideRevenue.Graduation Reward to Creator: The creator's fixed reward when their coin graduates.
SupplySideRevenue.Trader and Holder Rewards: The 0.25% leg paid straight out to traders on buys and coin holders on sells.

methodology.Fees: Everything paid to trade on Ride Markets, in USDC: a fee when a trade is opened, a fee when it settles, and the share of the profit paid to the caller who deployed the trade.

methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The opening and settlement fees, which the protocol keeps.

Fees.Trade Opening Fees: Charged when a trade is opened, based on its volume. Taken by the frontend as a direct USDC transfer to the fee wallet, outside the Trade Executor program, so it is counted only in transactions that invoke that program (including CPI `create_intent`) and only for what the settlement fees do not already account for.
Fees.Settlement Fees: Charged by the Trade Executor program when a trade settles: 0.7% of the USDC returned to the treasury, plus a cut of the caller's profit share.
Fees.Caller Profit Share: Paid out of the treasury's realised profit to the caller who deployed the trade, at a rate the DAO sets. The protocol sets and enforces this rate but does not receive it.

Revenue.Trade Opening Fees To Protocol: All trade opening fees are paid to the Ride Markets fee wallet.
Revenue.Settlement Fees To Protocol: All settlement fees are paid to the Ride Markets fee wallet.

ProtocolRevenue.Settlement Fees To Protocol: All settlement fees are paid to the Ride Markets fee wallet.

SupplySideRevenue.Caller Profit Share To Callers: Paid straight from the trade's proceeds to the caller, as the cost of sourcing the trade.

methodology.Fees: Swap fees charged on Hookers launches, in native ETH. A creator picks a launch style from the protocol's mechanism registry. The registry is read on chain, so styles added later are included automatically.
methodology.Revenue: The 30 bps protocol fee routed to FeeRouter, plus the share spent buying back and burning HKRS, the protocol's own token.

Buybacks on third-party launches are excluded and counted as supply side, since they accrue to those tokens' holders. Discretionary buybacks are funded from fees already counted as protocol revenue, so this figure overlaps ProtocolRevenue rather than adding to Revenue.

methodology.Fees: Everything borrowers pay: the flat fee charged when a loan is opened or extended, penalties paid when a loan is cured after its grace period, and the protocol's cut of any appreciation on yield-bearing collateral. Lodestar charges no interest, so nothing accrues over the life of a loan.
methodology.Revenue: The portion of the above kept by the protocol: the reserve cut of borrower fees, plus all penalties and all collateral yield skim.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The portion kept by the protocol, routed to the first-loss reserve that absorbs settlement shortfalls before lenders do.

Fees.Borrow Interest: One flat fee charged up front at origination and again on each extension, set by the term/LTV tier the borrower chose. It is netted out of the principal, so it is paid whether or not the loan is repaid.
Fees.Default Penalties: Charged when a borrower repays after the deadline's grace period, as a share of the principal being repaid, fixed at the rate in force when the loan was opened.
Fees.Collateral Yield Skim: A share of the appreciation on yield-bearing collateral (sFLR, stXRP) over the life of a loan, taken in the collateral token when it is returned. Recognised appreciation is capped at 20% per term, so an abnormal rate feed cannot inflate it.

Revenue.Borrow Interest: The reserve's cut of each borrower fee, being the fee less the amount locked for lenders.
Revenue.Default Penalties: All of it. Penalties are moved straight into the first-loss reserve.
Revenue.Collateral Yield Skim: All of it. The skim is transferred to the reserve in the collateral token.

ProtocolRevenue.Borrow Interest: The reserve's cut of each borrower fee, being the fee less the amount locked for lenders.
ProtocolRevenue.Default Penalties: All of it. Penalties are moved straight into the first-loss reserve.
ProtocolRevenue.Collateral Yield Skim: All of it. The skim is transferred to the reserve in the collateral token.

SupplySideRevenue.Borrow Interest: The lender share of each borrower fee, read from the amount the loan book locks in the pool for vesting. Lenders receive none of the penalties or the yield skim.

methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Loopr's 30% cut of each basket's mint fee, the LOOPR token creator + protocol tax paid to Loopr's own wallet, and ETH deposited into Loopr's community vault.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 70% of each basket's mint fee paid to that specific basket's own (possibly third-party, permissionless) creator.

Fees.Basket Mint Fees: Mint fee charged on LooprBasket index-token mints, paid in-kind in the basket's constituent tokens.
Fees.LOOPR Token Creator Tax: LOOPR token creator's and protocol's cut of the swap tax on LOOPR/ETH, both paid to Loopr's own wallet.
Fees.LOOPR Community Vault Deposits: ETH deposited into Loopr's LooprCommunityVault (sponsorships, partnerships, creator-tax sweeps).

Revenue.Basket Mint Fees To Loopr: Loopr protocol's 30% share of every basket's mint fee.
Revenue.LOOPR Token Creator Tax: LOOPR token creator's and protocol's cut of the swap tax, both paid to Loopr's own wallet.
Revenue.LOOPR Community Vault Deposits: ETH deposited into Loopr's LooprCommunityVault (sponsorships, partnerships, creator-tax sweeps).

ProtocolRevenue.Basket Mint Fees To Loopr: Loopr protocol's 30% share of every basket's mint fee.
ProtocolRevenue.LOOPR Token Creator Tax: LOOPR token creator's and protocol's cut of the swap tax, both paid to Loopr's own wallet.
ProtocolRevenue.LOOPR Community Vault Deposits: ETH deposited into Loopr's LooprCommunityVault (sponsorships, partnerships, creator-tax sweeps).

SupplySideRevenue.Basket Mint Fees To Basket Creators: The 70% of a basket's mint fee paid to that basket's own creator (permissionless — may not be Loopr itself).

methodology.Volume: Volume of all swaps on Pez's launch curves. Graduated pools trade on Uniswap v4 and are counted under the Uniswap v4 listing.
methodology.Fees: Pez curve trade fees and creator taxes on every launched token, plus the graduated Uniswap v4 pool fees of the PEZ platform token, realized through PoolFeesSwept events. Other graduated pools are counted under the Uniswap v4 listing. Pez's current deployment has no launch fee.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol revenue plus holders revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Any protocol fee share read from the on-chain fee policy (zero under the current policy), plus the creator fees and taxes of the PEZ token, which the Pez team launched and collects on.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: PEZ buyback-and-lock amounts reported by PoolFeesSwept for the PEZ pool. No such buyback has happened on-chain so far, so this is currently zero.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator fee, creator tax, and launched-token buyback amounts paid from curve fees of third-party launched tokens.

Fees.Curve Swap Fees: Base trade fees and creator taxes collected from swaps on Pez launch curves.
Fees.Token Swap Fees: Fees collected from Uniswap v4 swaps on the graduated PEZ pool, realized through PoolFeesSwept events.

Revenue.Curve Swap Fees to Protocol: Protocol share of curve swap fees defined by each token's launch fee policy.
Revenue.Token Swap Fees to Protocol: Protocol amount emitted by PoolFeesSwept for the PEZ pool.
Revenue.PEZ Creator Fees: Creator share of fees and taxes on the PEZ token, collected by the Pez team.
Revenue.Token Buy Back: PEZ buyback-and-lock amounts funded from PEZ trade fees.

ProtocolRevenue.Curve Swap Fees to Protocol: Protocol share of curve swap fees; zero under the current Pez policy.
ProtocolRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Protocol: Protocol amount emitted by PoolFeesSwept; zero under the current Pez policy.
ProtocolRevenue.PEZ Creator Fees: Creator share of fees and taxes on the PEZ token, collected by the Pez team.

HoldersRevenue.Token Buy Back: PEZ buyback-and-lock amounts funded from PEZ trade fees.

SupplySideRevenue.Curve Swap Fees to Creators: Creator share of curve swap fees on third-party tokens.
SupplySideRevenue.Curve Swap Fees to Meme Token Buybacks: Buyback share of curve swap fees used to buy third-party launched tokens.
SupplySideRevenue.Creator Tax: Creator tax collected on curve swaps of third-party tokens.

methodology.Volume: Output amount of every swap routed through the SwapOnHood aggregator contracts.
methodology.Fees: 0.25% protocol fee per swap, taken in ETH when ETH/WETH is on either side, otherwise in the output token.
methodology.Revenue: All fees (0.25% of the swap volume) go to the protocol treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All swap fees(0.25% of the swap volume) are retained by the protocol treasury.

Fees.Swap Fees: 0.25% protocol fee per swap routed through SwapOnHood.

Revenue.Swap Fees To Protocol: 0.25% protocol fee per swap, retained by the protocol treasury.

ProtocolRevenue.Swap Fees To Protocol: 0.25% protocol fee per swap, retained by the protocol treasury.

methodology.UserFees: Swap fees paid by traders. Locker distributions are not user fees.
methodology.Fees: Swap fees on the listed DLMM and DAMM factories plus WETH credited to U1 lockers. Excludes aggregator, keeper, flash-loan and liquidity-composition fees. DLMM uses SwapDetailed; DAMM uses changes in protocol and LP fee accumulators plus claims, in each historical fee token.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of swap fees accruing to the fee recipient, plus WETH credited to U1 lockers (including external funding).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Gross protocol swap-fee share accruing to the fee treasury.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Actual WETH distributions credited to U1 lockers by RewardsAdded, including external funding. Counted in Fees and Revenue at funding time, not again when users claim. No fixed forwarding percentage is assumed.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The share of swap fees that accrues to liquidity providers.
methodology.Volume: Sum of the input amount of every swap on Umbrae's DLMM (Liquidity Book style concentrated liquidity) and DAMM (dynamic-fee constant product) pools on Base. Pools are enumerated on chain from their factories and volume is read from each pool's swap events.

Fees.Token Swap Fees: Total swap fees charged by Umbrae DLMM and DAMM pools.
Fees.U1 Locker Distributions: WETH credited to U1 lockers, including external funding.

UserFees.Token Swap Fees: Total swap fees charged by Umbrae DLMM and DAMM pools, all of which is paid by traders.

Revenue.Swap Fees To Protocol: Protocol share of swap fees.
Revenue.U1 Locker Distributions: WETH credited to U1 lockers, including external funding.

ProtocolRevenue.Swap Fees To Protocol: Gross swap-fee accrual to the fee treasury.

HoldersRevenue.U1 Locker Distributions: WETH credited to U1 lockers at funding time, not again when users claim it.

SupplySideRevenue.Swap Fees To LPs: Liquidity provider share of swap fees.

methodology.Fees: AMM swap commission only: for each hourly volume_bucket on factory pairs (reflective + cumulative), fee = offer_volume * live pair.commission_rate (fee asset = offer asset). Excludes token_bonding wrap/unwrap and converter pairs. $WESO cw20_bonding curve tax_collected is cumulative-only (project_tax_pct 10) with no time-bucketed query, so curve taxes are NOT included. Buckets retain at most 168 hours.
methodology.Revenue: fee_collector_share_permille of the AMM commission (live per pair; sampled pairs are 1000 = 100%) sent to fee_collector terra1wkdm6wcm4srahrvp09jea7csfq3yuacc4gmyft6p6n6pls9wy5js9lqhqq. No separate LP share of this commission field is counted — reflective pools may compensate LPs via the curve, not this commission — so SupplySideRevenue is omitted.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue: at current on-chain shares the counted AMM commission accrues to the fee collector / protocol.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Liquidity providers revenue

Fees.Token Swap Fees: Offer-side swap volume × live pair.commission_rate from WESO AMM volume_buckets. Does not include $WESO bonding-curve taxes (cumulative tax_collected only).

Revenue.Swap Fees To Protocol: fee_collector_share_permille of AMM commission (1000 on sampled pairs) to the fee collector.

ProtocolRevenue.Swap Fees To Protocol: fee_collector_share_permille of AMM commission (1000 on sampled pairs) to the fee collector.

methodology.Fees: Trading commission collected on perp trades (funding payments excluded).
methodology.Revenue: Trading commission retained by the protocol after referral rebates (fees − rebates).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Trading commission retained by the Jetbit protocol treasury (fees − referral rebates).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Referral rebates — trading commission paid back out to referrers.
methodology.Volume: Real perpetual-futures notional (filled_quantity x filled_price) from Jetbit's public aggregate feed; copy-trade mirror volume and display padding are excluded.
methodology.OpenInterest: Live notional of all open positions (Σ |quantity| × mark price across open main and copy-trade positions), in USD, from Jetbit's public feed.

Fees.Trading Fees: Trading commission charged on perp trades.

SupplySideRevenue.Trading Fees To Referrers: Share of trading commission paid back out to referrers.

Revenue.Trading Fees To Protocol: Trading commission retained by the protocol after referral rebates.

ProtocolRevenue.Trading Fees To Protocol: Trading commission retained by the Jetbit protocol treasury after referral rebates.

methodology.Fees: Taker trading fees: each market's taker_fee_ppm (0.1% on most markets) applied to that market's volume. Maker fees are not charged to takers and are excluded.
methodology.Revenue: All trading fees are collected by the protocol. Partner commissions and trader fee rebates are paid from the treasury after the fact and are not netted here.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue: the protocol treasury receives all trading fees.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LPs revenue
methodology.Volume: Taker volume of all perpetual fills on the TRUE DEX venue (one fill counted once), summed per UTC day from the venue trade tape.

Revenue.Perp Trading Fees: Taker fees on perpetual fills, kept by the protocol treasury.

ProtocolRevenue.Perp Trading Fees: Taker fees on perpetual fills, kept by the protocol treasury.

methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees; traders pay all three components.
methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by traders on the protocol's BUCKET/ETH Uniswap v4 pool: the 1% LP fee plus the BucketFeeHook's 3% Treasury fee (FEE_BPS is a verified on-chain constant), both measured on the ETH leg of each Swap event; plus the Stockback router's 0.5% input fee (exact per-swap amount from its Swapped event).
methodology.Revenue: The hook's 3% Treasury fee, the 1% LP fee (the pool's liquidity is protocol-owned and permanently locked), and the protocol half of Stockback router fees.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The 1% LP fee, accruing to the protocol's permanently locked liquidity position.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The trader's half of every Stockback router fee, credited back as stock rewards.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The hook's 3% Treasury fee plus the protocol half of router fees: this is the stream the payout engine converts into tokenized stocks delivered to BUCKET holder wallets. Keeper gas for those deliveries is paid from this stream and varies with chain conditions; it is not modeled as a fixed split.

Fees.BUCKET Pool LP Fees: 1% LP fee on the protocol-owned BUCKET/ETH Uniswap v4 pool, measured on the ETH leg of each Swap event.
Fees.BucketFeeHook Treasury Fee: 3% Treasury fee (FEE_BPS = 300, verified on-chain constant) charged by the BucketFeeHook on each pool swap, measured on the ETH leg.
Fees.Stockback Router Fees: 0.5% fee on the input of swaps routed through the Stockback router (exact per-swap amount from its Swapped event).

Revenue.BUCKET Pool LP Fees To Protocol: 1% LP fee accruing to the protocol's permanently locked liquidity position.
Revenue.BucketFeeHook Treasury Fee To Holders: 3% Treasury fee that funds the payout engine for BUCKET holder distributions.
Revenue.Stockback Router Fees To Holders: Protocol's half of each Stockback router fee, funding holder payouts.

ProtocolRevenue.BUCKET Pool LP Fees To Protocol: 1% LP fee accruing to the protocol's permanently locked liquidity position.

HoldersRevenue.BucketFeeHook Treasury Fee To Holders: 3% Treasury fee converted into tokenized stocks delivered to BUCKET holder wallets.
HoldersRevenue.Stockback Router Fees To Holders: Protocol's half of each Stockback router fee, funding holder payouts.

SupplySideRevenue.Stockback Router Fees To Traders: Trader's half of each Stockback router fee, credited back as stock rewards.

methodology.Volume: Sum of every buy and sell on Fox Brokers bonding curves (Buy/Sell events on curve contracts created by the launch factories), valued in USD with the protocol's on-chain oracle price of the curve's quote asset (a Robinhood Stock Token or WETH). Post-graduation SushiSwap V3 trading is not included here (it is tracked under SushiSwap).
methodology.Fees: Trading fees charged on every curve buy and sell (1% of the quote amount on the active preset: 0.8% creator, 0.2% protocol).
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: paid by traders on curve trades.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol share of curve trading fees (0.2%).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Protocol share of curve trading fees (0.2%).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator share of curve trading fees (0.8%), paid to the token creator's fee recipient.

Fees.Token Swap Fees: Trading fees charged on every curve buy and sell (1% of the quote amount on the active preset).

UserFees.Token Swap Fees: Same as Fees: paid by traders on curve trades.

Revenue.Token Swap Fees To Protocol: Protocol share of curve trading fees (0.2%).

ProtocolRevenue.Token Swap Fees To Protocol: Protocol share of curve trading fees (0.2%).

SupplySideRevenue.Token Swap Fees To Creators: Creator share of curve trading fees (0.8%), paid to the token creator's fee recipient.

methodology.Volume: Gross native SHIDO notional from Trade.nativeAmount on the production v2 bonding-curve factory, counting one side of each buy/sell. Buy refunds are excluded. No legacy-factory activity, BubbleSwap/router activity, post-graduation Shido DEX trading, LP activity or graduation liquidity is counted.
methodology.Fees: Actual protocol and creator trading fees from Trade, plus the graduationFee from Graduated. Accrual basis in native SHIDO, valued using its 1:1 WSHIDO wrapper. No fixed fee-rate estimates, claim double-counting, gas fees or post-graduation fees.
methodology.UserFees: Protocol and creator trading fees directly paid by bonding-curve traders. Graduation fees are excluded because they are deducted from the curve reserve before migration rather than charged directly to an end-user.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol trading fees plus graduation fees, excluding the creator trading-fee share and all post-graduation revenue.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue (protocol trading fees + graduation fees): fees allocated to the protocol when accrued at the factory. Subsequent treasury spending or announced buybacks are not measured by this adapter.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator trading fees accrued by Trade events. This is creator income, not LP fees or revenue of holders of the Bubble Protocol token.

Fees.Bonding Curve Trading Fees: Protocol and creator trading fees emitted by the production factory's Trade events, accrued when each trade executes regardless of when claimed.
Fees.Graduation Fees: The graduationFee emitted by Graduated, deducted from the curve's native reserve before DEX liquidity is created.

UserFees.Bonding Curve Trading Fees: Protocol and creator trading fees directly paid by bonding-curve traders.

Revenue.Bonding Curve Trading Fees To Protocol: Only the protocolFee component of Trade events, excluding creator fees.
Revenue.Graduation Fees To Protocol: The full graduationFee component of Graduated events, accrued to the protocol.

ProtocolRevenue.Bonding Curve Trading Fees To Protocol: Only the protocolFee component of Trade events, excluding creator fees.
ProtocolRevenue.Graduation Fees To Protocol: The full graduationFee component of Graduated events, accrued to the protocol.

SupplySideRevenue.Bonding Curve Trading Fees To Creators: The creatorFee component emitted for every bonding-curve trade, whether already claimed or still claimable.

methodology.Fees: The protocol fee taken from every round's tile deposits (10% at launch, read per round from the RoundClosed event) plus the full winning bid of every weekly tile ad auction, paid in SOL or ATTN. Player deposits are paid out to winning bidders and are not counted.
methodology.UserFees: The round protocol fee paid by tile bidders plus the winning ad auction bids paid by advertisers in SOL or ATTN.
methodology.Revenue: The round protocol fee plus 10% of each winning SOL ad bid and all of each winning ATTN ad bid, sent to the protocol treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All revenue stays in the protocol treasury; its use (buybacks, staking rewards, build budget) is decided off-chain and not tracked here.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 90% of each winning SOL ad bid forwarded into that tile's jackpot vault, paid to the tile's bidders on a jackpot hit.

Fees.Round Protocol Fee: Protocol fee taken from each round's tile deposits at close (10% at launch, snapshotted per round).
Fees.Ad Auction Bids: Winning bid of each weekly tile ad auction at settlement, in SOL or ATTN.

Revenue.Round Protocol Fee To Treasury: Round protocol fee sent to the protocol treasury.
Revenue.Ad Auction Fee To Treasury: 10% of each winning SOL ad bid and 100% of each winning ATTN ad bid sent to the protocol treasury.

ProtocolRevenue.Round Protocol Fee To Treasury: Round protocol fee sent to the protocol treasury.
ProtocolRevenue.Ad Auction Fee To Treasury: 10% of each winning SOL ad bid and 100% of each winning ATTN ad bid sent to the protocol treasury.

SupplySideRevenue.Ad Auction Bids To Tile Jackpots: 90% of each winning SOL ad bid forwarded into that tile's jackpot vault.

methodology.Volume: Notional volume of Hyperliquid trades routed through AlphaPilot's builder code.
methodology.Fees: Builder code fees paid on Hyperliquid trades routed through AlphaPilot; excludes Hyperliquid exchange trading fees.
methodology.Revenue: Builder code fees collected by AlphaPilot from Hyperliquid trades.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Builder code fees collected by AlphaPilot from Hyperliquid trades.

Revenue.Hyperliquid Builder Code Fees: Builder code fees collected by the builder.

ProtocolRevenue.Hyperliquid Builder Code Fees: Builder code fees collected by the builder.

methodology.UserFees: Users pay fees on each swap.
methodology.Fees: Users pay fees on each swap.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol receives 20% of the fees paid by users.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol receives 20% of the fees paid by users.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 80% of user jetton fees are distributed among LPs, based on the amount of user liquidity utilized in a particular swap.

methodology.Fees: Native ETH creator rewards claimed from PonsV2FeeEscrow for World is Flat ($WIF).
methodology.Revenue: 100% of claimed Pons creator rewards are retained by the WIF treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All claimed Pons creator rewards flow to the WIF treasury.

Fees.Pons Creator Rewards: Creator share of Pons swap fees on the $WIF pool, claimed from PonsV2FeeEscrow.

Revenue.Pons Creator Rewards: Claimed Pons creator rewards retained by the WIF treasury.

ProtocolRevenue.Pons Creator Rewards: Claimed Pons creator rewards retained by the WIF treasury.

methodology.Fees: Everything borrowers and traders pay on gage: the deal or origination fee taken when a loan funds, trade fees on sold reclaim rights and lender units, the cash-out platform fee, and the borrower's fixed cost paid to lenders at repayment (repayment cap minus principal). Fixed-cost loans have no interest accrual: the cost is booked when the loan is repaid.
methodology.Revenue: Deal, origination, trade and cash-out fees, plus the Earn performance fee on lender returns.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The Earn performance fee (curator and protocol shares).
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The borrower's fixed cost paid to lenders at repayment, before the Earn performance fee for loans an Earn strategy funded.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Deal, origination, trade and cash-out fees: since D57 every one of them buys GAGE for the permanent GAGE-only floor bands of the GAGE/sGAGE pool.

Fees.Deal and origination fees: 1% of funded principal on legacy vaults; the registry feeBps of principal on V2 engines, charged at activation.
Fees.Trade and cash-out fees: The registry trade fee on a sold reclaim right or lender unit; 0.5% of remaining proceeds on a cash-out.
Fees.Borrower cost paid to lenders: Repayment cap minus funded principal, paid to the lender when the borrower reclaims.

Revenue.Deal and origination fees: Routed to the GAGE floor through DealFeeRouter.
Revenue.Trade and cash-out fees: Routed to the GAGE floor through DealFeeRouter.
Revenue.Earn performance fee: feeBps of a settled loan's return; the protocol share goes to the deal fee router, the rest to the curator.

HoldersRevenue.Deal and origination fees: Deal and origination fees buy GAGE for the permanent GAGE-only floor bands of the GAGE/sGAGE pool.
HoldersRevenue.Trade and cash-out fees: Trade and cash-out fees buy GAGE for the permanent GAGE-only floor bands of the GAGE/sGAGE pool.

ProtocolRevenue.Earn performance fee: The Earn performance fee, covering both the protocol share sent to the deal fee router and the curator share.

SupplySideRevenue.Borrower cost paid to lenders: Repayment cap minus funded principal, paid to the lender when the borrower reclaims, before the Earn performance fee.

methodology.Fees: The protocol fee on every referral bounty that pays out: 10% of the reward, paid by the referrer.
methodology.Revenue: All protocol fees (10% of referral rewards) go to the ref_market treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All protocol fees (10% of referral rewards) go to the ref_market treasury.

Fees.Referral Payout Fees: 10% protocol fee on every referral bounty that pays out, charged to the referrer.

Revenue.Referral Payout Fees To Treasury: All referral payout fees go to the ref_market treasury.

ProtocolRevenue.Referral Payout Fees To Treasury: All referral payout fees go to the ref_market treasury.

methodology.Volume: Volume of bonding-curve (pre-graduation) swaps on Cook Market launched pools, measured in the pool's pair token. Post-graduation Uniswap v4 volume is excluded.
methodology.Fees: Swap fees (1% of the swap) and optional creator tax charged by the Cook hook on every swap, before and after graduation, there is no launch fee
methodology.Revenue: Part of the swap fees (protocolFeeShareBps, 10% at launch) sent to the Cook treasury
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Part of the swap fees (protocolFeeShareBps, 10% at launch) sent to the Cook treasury
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Remaining swap fees and 100% of the creator tax paid to token creators

Fees.Curve Swap Fees: Fees and taxes collected from swaps while the pool is still in its bonding-curve phase
Fees.Token Swap Fees: Fees and taxes collected from swaps on graduated pools

Revenue.Curve Swap Fees to Protocol: Part of (protocolFeeShareBps, 10% at launch) the curve swap fees collected goes to the protocol treasury
Revenue.Token Swap Fees to Protocol: Part of (protocolFeeShareBps, 10% at launch) the graduated pool swap fees collected goes to the protocol treasury

ProtocolRevenue.Curve Swap Fees to Protocol: Part of (protocolFeeShareBps, 10% at launch) the curve swap fees collected goes to the protocol treasury
ProtocolRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Protocol: Part of (protocolFeeShareBps, 10% at launch) the graduated pool swap fees collected goes to the protocol treasury

SupplySideRevenue.Curve Swap Fees to Creators: Part of (90% at launch) the curve swap fees collected goes to the creators
SupplySideRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Creators: Part of (90% at launch) the graduated pool swap fees collected goes to the creators
SupplySideRevenue.Creator Tax: Optional tax (0-10%, chosen per launch) on every swap, paid entirely to the creator

methodology.Fees: Includes 2% property NFT sale fees and interest earned from property NFTs.
methodology.Revenue: Includes 2% property NFT sale fees and 10% of interest earned from property NFTs.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Includes 2% property NFT sale fees and 10% of interest earned from property NFTs.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Includes 90% of interest earned from property NFTs paid to NFT owners.

Fees.Property Sale Fees: 2% of the sale price of the property NFT.
Fees.Property Interest: Net interest earned on property NFTs realised during redemption.

Revenue.Property Sale Fees to Protocol: 2% of the sale price of the property NFT.
Revenue.Property Interest to Protocol: 10% of interest earned on property NFTs realised during redemption.

ProtocolRevenue.Property Sale Fees to Protocol: 2% of the sale price of the property NFT.
ProtocolRevenue.Property Interest to Protocol: 10% of interest earned on property NFTs realised during redemption.

SupplySideRevenue.Property Interest to NFT Owners: 90% of interest earned on property NFTs realised during redemption.

methodology.Fees: The tax BaseStonk's Uniswap v4 hook takes on every swap in a launched token's pool, from the hook's FeeTaken event. Each launch sets its own buy and sell rate. A buy pays the tax in the launch token and a sell in the pair; token-denominated amounts are converted into the pair at the pool price the same transaction's Swap reports.
methodology.Revenue: The platform's cut of the tax plus what reaches BSTONK holders: half the tax capped at 1% of the trade to the treasury, any part of the creator's cut the payee list left unplaced and the hook swept to the treasury, and the share of the creator's cut paid to BSTONK's dividend distributor, to the BSTONK basket vault, or burnt as BSTONK.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The treasury's take: half the tax capped at 1% of the trade, plus unplaced creator fees swept to it.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Value to BSTONK holders, paid by the hook in the transaction the fee was taken: BSTONK's own pool pays its creator cut to BSTONK's dividend distributor and burns half of it, and launches carry the BSTONK basket vault as a payee; the vault pays BSTONK holders in rounds. Base only - BSTONK lives on Base.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The creator's cut of the tax less what the treasury swept and what reached BSTONK holders: the creator's wallets, the launch token's own holders through its dividend distributor, the burn of the launch token and the hook-owned liquidity wedge, as each launch configured them.
methodology.Volume: The pair side of every swap in a taxed pool, including the creator's dev buy at launch and excluding the hook's own buyback and liquidity swaps. Counted under Uniswap v4 as well.

Fees.Token Swap Fees: The hook's tax on each swap in a launched token's pool, at the launch's buy or sell rate.

Revenue.Swap Fees To Treasury: The platform's cut of the tax: half of it, capped at 1% of the trade, paid to the treasury.
Revenue.Unplaced Creator Fees To Treasury: The part of the creator's cut the launch's payee list left unplaced, swept to the treasury.
Revenue.Swap Fees To BSTONK Holders: The creator cut of BSTONK's own pool, paid to BSTONK's dividend distributor.
Revenue.Basket Dividends To BSTONK Holders: Paid by the hook to the BSTONK basket vault as a payee on launches.
Revenue.BSTONK Burn: BSTONK the hook burnt from BSTONK's own pool: the launch token on buys, bought back on sells.

ProtocolRevenue.Swap Fees To Treasury: The platform's cut of the tax: half of it, capped at 1% of the trade, paid to the treasury.
ProtocolRevenue.Unplaced Creator Fees To Treasury: The part of the creator's cut the launch's payee list left unplaced, swept to the treasury.

HoldersRevenue.Swap Fees To BSTONK Holders: The creator cut of BSTONK's own pool, paid to BSTONK's dividend distributor.
HoldersRevenue.Basket Dividends To BSTONK Holders: Paid by the hook to the BSTONK basket vault as a payee on launches.
HoldersRevenue.BSTONK Burn: BSTONK the hook burnt from BSTONK's own pool: the launch token on buys, bought back on sells.

SupplySideRevenue.Swap Fees To Creators And Token Holders: The creator's cut after the treasury's sweep and BSTONK holders' share: creator wallets, the token's own holders, its burn and its liquidity wedge.

methodology.Fees: Gross LP trading fees claimed by Valhalla-managed Meteora DLMM positions. Each public Meteora claim event is counted only when its transaction contains Valhalla's matching post-workflow management-fee transfer; claim assets are measured directly, not inferred from a fee rate. DAMM v2 and opening fees are excluded.

Fees.Meteora DLMM LP Fees Claimed: Gross LP trading fees paid out by decoded Meteora DLMM claim events in attributable Valhalla transactions.

methodology.Fees: 0.35% redeem fee on private transfers (withheld from the gross amount before zAssets are minted to the recipient, live since 2026-06-02) plus liquidity-based unwrap fees charged by the LiquidityManagers.
methodology.Revenue: All fees (redeem and unwrap) are retained by the protocol: the redeem fee is never minted, and unwrap fees accrue to the LiquidityManager fee surplus.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All fees (redeem and unwrap) are retained by the protocol.

Fees.Redeem Fees: 0.35% of the gross private-transfer amount, derived from Teleport mints as minted * 0.35 / 99.65.
Fees.Unwrap Fees: feeAmount from LiquidityManager Unwrapped events; the rate rises as liquidity falls below target (zBNB is exempt).

methodology.Fees: Everything users pay the protocol: the price of every cat minted, the trading fee the hook takes on the $HASH pool, and the secondary-market royalty the collection routes to the hook. The mint price is derived per cat from the contract's own curve - the number of cats created so far times PRICE_STEP - rather than read from a transaction value, so a mint sent with excess ether cannot inflate it.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees. Every one of the three flows is paid by a user: the miner pays the entry price, the trader pays the swap fee, and the secondary-market buyer pays the royalty.
methodology.Revenue: Fees minus the rent paid out to living cats.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Rent paid to the cats already alive. Every mint splits its price between the cats that came before it and the hook; cat holders are suppliers whose asset earns, not holders of a governance token, so their cut is a cost of revenue. Measured as the mint price minus the hook's cut, which is exact and needs no reconstruction from the rent accumulator. The hook's cut is what it was owed in the window rather than what it was sent: a transfer that fails its gas stipend is held in the collection's hookDue and forwarded later, so the change in that balance is added back.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: The share of revenue that joins the hook's buyback queue and is spent buying $HASH back on the pool and burning it. Measured at the fee source - the moment the hook receives and splits the money - rather than when a buyback executes, since the queue is drained gradually under a per-block cap.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The developer's share of revenue, at the hook's devBps rate, read from the chain rather than hardcoded.

Fees.Mint/Redeem Fees: The price paid for every cat mined in the window, derived per cat from the contract's price curve.
Fees.Token Swap Fees: The trading fee the hook takes on $HASH swaps. The pool's own fee is zero, so this is the whole of it. The rate decays from its opening value to its target over the first ten minutes of trading, so the amounts are read from FeeTaken rather than computed.
Fees.Creator Fees: Secondary-market royalties, which the collection routes to the hook as the ERC-2981 recipient - in ether, or in WETH when the sale settled in WETH.

UserFees.Mint/Redeem Fees: The price paid for every cat mined in the window.
UserFees.Token Swap Fees: The trading fee paid by swappers on the $HASH pool.

Revenue.Token Buy Back: The part of revenue that joins the buyback queue.
Revenue.Protocol Fees: The developer's share of revenue, at the hook's devBps rate.

SupplySideRevenue.Rent to Cat Holders: Rent accrued to the cats alive at the time of each mint, paid out of that mint's price.

HoldersRevenue.Token Buy Back: Ether queued for buying $HASH back on the pool and burning it.

ProtocolRevenue.Protocol Fees: The developer's share of everything the hook receives.

methodology.Volume: USDC wagered: both stakes of every market at the moment they lock into escrow (a market is only created on-chain once fully matched). This is betting volume, not deposits — funding a balance is not counted, only money committed to a bet. Each dollar is counted exactly once: the two stakes come from two different bettors, so this is the pot, not the maker/taker double count an orderbook has to halve. Cancelled markets refund the stakes, but the matched notional stays counted, in line with other prediction markets.

methodology.Fees: Sum of `fee` fields from `OptionExercised` (settlement fee on each exercised leg) and `PositionClosed` (matched-pair close fee). Both are charged at `1 / sf_fee_divisor` of the exercised/closed collateral and paid in USDC.
methodology.Revenue: Equal to Fees (sum of `OptionExercised` and `PositionClosed` fees): the protocol has no governance token, and every fee is transferred to the on-chain `feeCollector_address` (which the owner can rotate via `setFeeCollector` / `FeeCollectorChanged`).
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Equal to Fees (sum of `OptionExercised` and `PositionClosed` fees): the protocol has no governance token, and every fee is transferred to the on-chain `feeCollector_address` (which the owner can rotate via `setFeeCollector` / `FeeCollectorChanged`).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Fees going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LPs revenue
methodology.NotionalVolume: Sum of `amount` from each `optionIssued` event on StochasticOptions: USDC collateral committed by writers when minting a paired (long + short) position. Following the Prodigy/Dopex/Rysk convention of counting raw token amount (no oracle multiplication), this is the unit count of options minted — `1 USDC = 1 option unit` per protocol design.
methodology.PremiumVolume: Sum of USDC paid by option buyers on SFSwapV0Pair AMM pools, direction USDC→tradeToken only (the `amount0In` field of each `Swap` event). The reverse direction (tradeToken→USDC) is a writer unwinding their previously-sold leg and does not count as new premium inflow. Pair addresses are discovered from `PairCreated` events on the factory (one-time event per (token, tokenId) tuple).

Fees.Option Exercise Fee: Settlement fee on each leg exercised via `OptionExercised`. Computed as `1 / sf_fee_divisor` of the collateral burned and transferred to `feeCollector_address`.
Fees.Option Close Fee: Matched-pair close fee on each leg unwound via `PositionClosed`. Same rate as the exercise fee (so this is not a cheaper substitute for `exercise`) and transferred to `feeCollector_address`.

Revenue.Option Exercise Fee: Exercise settlement fees routed to the on-chain `feeCollector_address`.
Revenue.Option Close Fee: Matched-pair close fees routed to the on-chain `feeCollector_address`.

ProtocolRevenue.Option Exercise Fee: Exercise settlement fees routed to the on-chain `feeCollector_address`.
ProtocolRevenue.Option Close Fee: Matched-pair close fees routed to the on-chain `feeCollector_address`.

SupplySideRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Creators: Creator share of the graduated pool swap fees (70% at deployment).

methodology.Fees: Trading fees from Peach bonding-curve trades and the launchpad's cut of graduated-pool LP fees, including creator tax, counted once when the fee accrues. Fees without a USD price are excluded.
methodology.Revenue: The platform's own share of fees, after creator, partner, referral and launched-token buyback shares.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue - all of it goes to the protocol.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Creator, partner and referral shares of fees, plus the share allocated to launched-token buybacks. These launched tokens are not the Peach governance token.

Fees.Bonding trading fees: The total_fee amount of canonical BONDING allocations, including the recorded base, protection and creator fees.
Fees.Graduated pool allocations: The total_fee amount of canonical LP allocations. This is the launchpad allocation, not every third-party LP fee in the whole pool.

Revenue.Platform allocations: The recorded platform_amount (platformNet/protocolNet) after the event-specific split.

SupplySideRevenue.Creator allocations: Creator amount including creator tax and any routing to a launched-token holder distributor.
SupplySideRevenue.Partner allocations: Partner amount from each allocation event.
SupplySideRevenue.Referral allocations: Referrer amount from each allocation event.
SupplySideRevenue.Launched-token buyback budgets: Share of collected trading fees allocated to launched-token buybacks at accrual; included in gross fees and supply-side revenue. Subsequent releases are excluded. These launched tokens are not the launchpad governance token.

methodology.Fees: Everything traders pay copyfomo on every copied buy and sell (a 2% service fee plus the gas copyfomo fronts for them, billed back as one stablecoin transfer to the copyfomo treasury, counted on the day the fee is collected), plus the creator fees of the copyfomo token $COPY: the Pons launchpad hook takes 3% of every swap of the COPY/COIN pool on Robinhood Chain, of which 2.7% goes to the creator (1% hook fee, 70% to the creator, plus a 2% creator tax). Counted on the day of the trade, valued at the hourly COIN price. The fees are swept into COIN by Pons and claimed by copyfomo in batches later; the claims are not what is counted.
methodology.UserFees: The part paid by copyfomo users: service fee plus gas billed back. Excludes the $COPY creator fees, which are paid by $COPY traders.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Referral rewards paid to copyfomo referrers, plus the actual on-chain cost copyfomo pays on users' behalf: the EVM bundler gas and the SOL spent by the Solana fee payer (transaction fees and token-account rent).
methodology.Revenue: Fees minus SupplySideRevenue, i.e. after the EVM bundler gas, the Solana fee payer cost and referral rewards: the service fee plus copyfomo's margin on gas, plus the $COPY creator fees (the 'token fees' figure on copyfomo.com/data). The 'protocol fees, after gas' figure on copyfomo.com/data is the service part before referral rewards.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Buyback & burn of $COPY, funded by the creator fees: what the copyfomo creator wallets pay (COIN or USDG) in every transaction where they buy $COPY from the pool and burn $COPY in the same transaction (the buyback account buys and burns in one user operation). Counted on the day of the buy, which follows the trades that generated the fees. A holder cashback leg (USDG distributed to $COPY holders) is planned and will be added when it goes live.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Revenue minus HoldersRevenue: service revenue and the creator fees kept by copyfomo.

Fees.Treasury inflow: Every stablecoin transfer into the copyfomo treasury. The service fee and the gas billed back to the trader arrive together in one transfer and cannot be split on-chain.
Fees.$COPY creator fees: 2.7% of the COIN leg of every swap of the COPY/COIN Uniswap v4 pool on Robinhood Chain (PoolManager Swap events of the pool), valued at the hourly COIN price on Dune. Rate from the hook's launch config: 1% hook fee with 70% to the creator, plus a 2% creator tax.

UserFees.Treasury inflow: Same as the Fees component: everything copyfomo users pay.

SupplySideRevenue.Referral rewards: USDC sent by the copyfomo referral payout wallet on Base to referrers (its top-ups from the treasury are internal and excluded), plus any stablecoin sent by the treasury back to identified copyfomo user wallets.
SupplySideRevenue.Bundler gas cost: Gas the copyfomo bundler wallets paid to the ERC-4337 EntryPoint for users' operations, priced with the daily WETH / WBNB price.
SupplySideRevenue.Solana fee payer cost: SOL spent by the copyfomo Solana fee payer, which signs every copyfomo Solana transaction: signature fees and the rent of the token accounts it creates, net of rent returned on close (its balance change in its own transactions, excluding its top-ups co-signed by the Solana treasury), priced with the daily SOL price.

HoldersRevenue.Buyback & burn: COIN and USDG sent by the copyfomo creator wallets in every transaction that swaps on the COPY/COIN pool, delivers $COPY to them and burns $COPY from them (Transfer to the zero address) in that same transaction, since 2026-09-11 when the buyback programme started. The three manual buys of 2026-09-11, burned the next day in one transaction (hash in the query helper), are listed explicitly.

Revenue.Treasury inflow: Same as the Fees component: gross service fees before the supply-side deductions.
Revenue.$COPY creator fees: Same as the Fees component: creator fees have no supply-side share.
Revenue.Referral rewards: Same as the SupplySideRevenue component, subtracted from gross fees.
Revenue.Bundler gas cost: Same as the SupplySideRevenue component, subtracted from gross fees.
Revenue.Solana fee payer cost: Same as the SupplySideRevenue component, subtracted from gross fees.

ProtocolRevenue.Buyback & burn: Same as the HoldersRevenue component, subtracted from Revenue.

methodology.Fees: Fees paid by users on heks: a fee on every swap in a launched coin's pool, plus the flat fee a creator pays to launch one. The swap fee is charged in the pool's pair asset. It is the protocol fee — 1% in steady state, higher in a launch's first ten seconds to price out snipers — plus, on coins launched from V2.2 whose creator set one, a creator tax of up to 10%. Both are read from the vault's own events: Collected carries the protocol fee and its split, TaxCredited the creator tax.
methodology.UserFees: All fees are paid by users: the swap fee and the creator tax by traders, the launch fee by the creator.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's 30% share of every swap's protocol fee, plus the launch fee in full. The creator tax is never shared with the protocol.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol's 30% share of every swap's protocol fee, plus the launch fee in full. There is no heks token, so none of this is distributed to holders.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The 70% of every swap's protocol fee that goes to the coin's creator, plus the creator tax in full on coins that set one. A creator can redirect both to the holders of their own coin at launch; they leave the protocol either way.

Fees.Token Swap Fees: The protocol fee on each swap, charged in the pool's pair asset: 1% in steady state. For the first ten seconds after a launch it is higher, which prices out snipers of the opening block: up to V2.1 it decays linearly from 80% to 1%; from V2.2 buys pay a surcharge that starts at 99% of the trade and halves down to zero, and the buyer always keeps at least 1%.
Fees.Creator Tax: From V2.2: a tax of up to 10% a creator may set at launch, paid by traders on top of the protocol fee.
Fees.Launch Fees: Flat fee in native ETH paid by the creator when a coin is launched.

UserFees.Token Swap Fees: The protocol fee on each swap, paid by the trader in the pool's pair asset.
UserFees.Creator Tax: From V2.2: the creator's own tax, paid by the trader in the pool's pair asset.
UserFees.Launch Fees: Flat fee in native ETH paid by the creator when a coin is launched.

Revenue.Token Swap Fees to Protocol: The protocol's 30% share of each swap's protocol fee.
Revenue.Launch Fees to Protocol: Flat launch fee, kept in full by the protocol.

ProtocolRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Protocol: The protocol's 30% share of each swap's protocol fee.
ProtocolRevenue.Launch Fees to Protocol: Flat launch fee, kept in full by the protocol.

SupplySideRevenue.Creator Fees: The 70% of each swap's protocol fee paid out to the coin's creator, or to the holders of their coin if the creator chose that at launch.
SupplySideRevenue.Creator Tax: From V2.2: the creator tax in full, to the creator or to the coin's holders.

methodology.Fees: Actual MON fees accrued to the protocol treasury and sent to the buyback vault at round settlement, plus separately paid auto-bet gas subsidies. Excludes MON allocated back to players and does not count gross stakes as fees.
methodology.Revenue: MON round settlement fees retained by the treasury and buyback vault; excludes auto-bet execution fees paid to the gas-subsidy wallet.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: User-paid auto-bet execution fees transferred to the execution wallet as gas subsidies, included in Fees but excluded from Revenue; measures the subsidy paid, not actual transaction gas expenditure.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: MON round fees allocated directly to the protocol treasury; excludes gas subsidies, the separate buyback budget and GONE inventory valuations.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Successful GONE staking rewards funded by the buyback vault, valued in MON at the matching buyback's actual execution rate (MON spent / GONE bought), then priced in USD by the SDK. Includes pending rewards only when successfully funded; excludes mining allocations, no-staker treasury diversions, other funders and later claims. Execution-price valuation includes trading costs and is not an independent GONE market price.

Fees.Round Fees To Treasury: Actual MON accrued to the round treasury in ProtocolTreasuryAccrued.amount.
Fees.Round Fees To Buyback Vault: Actual MON sent to the buyback vault in BuybackFeeDistributed.amount, including the remaining pot when no winning stake exists.
Fees.Auto-Bet Execution Fees: The fee field of each successful AutoBetExecuted event.

Revenue.Round Fees To Treasury: Actual MON accrued to the round treasury in ProtocolTreasuryAccrued.amount.

ProtocolRevenue.Round Fees To Treasury: Actual MON accrued to the round treasury in ProtocolTreasuryAccrued.amount.

HoldersRevenue.GONE Staking Rewards At Buyback Executio: RewardFunded.amount from the buyback vault multiplied by the matching BuybackExecuted.monAmount / goneAmount. Match by transaction and log order; round down to MON wei per funding event. Pending rewards use the successful funding transaction's rate.

SupplySideRevenue.Trading Fees to Launched Token Holders: 12% of collected fees, booked to the launched token's holder-reward vault.
SupplySideRevenue.Trading Fees to Project Token Buyback: 5% of collected fees, spent buying back and burning the launched token.

Fees.Referral Fees: The referrer's share of the swap fee, USDC-denominated leg only.

methodology.Fees: The fee a V5 or V6 launch pool charges on each trade, taken by that launch's hook inside the swap itself and read from the hook's own event, so the rate is never assumed here. It is 1% at regime; an anti-sniper launch charges more on buys during its opening window, on a curve that decays over the first blocks - 95%, then 70%, 40% and 10% - before settling at the same 1%, while sells in that window pay the regime rate. The fee is taken in either the launched token or its quote asset, whichever side the trader paid in. Both generations are read: V6 only took over new launches, it did not stop V5's existing pools from trading. V1-V4 legacy launches (pre-hook, plain Uniswap v3 with a per-launch lock contract) are not covered.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of each fee, which is a split of the fee and not a rate on the trade: it keeps 50% under the default split, 30% when the launch opted into Holder Rewards, and 10% of any fee taken during a launch's opening window, which has its own fixed split. All three are set by the contract and not adjustable after launch.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The protocol's share of each fee, which is a split of the fee and not a rate on the trade: it keeps 50% under the default split, 30% when the launch opted into Holder Rewards, and 10% of any fee taken during a launch's opening window, which has its own fixed split. All three are set by the contract and not adjustable after launch.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Everything not kept by the protocol: the creator's share, the remainder streamed to the launched token's own holders via the Reward Vault on Holder-Rewards launches, and - on fees taken during the opening window - the 80% earmarked to the launch's Treasury Reserve, which buys the launched token back to burn it.

Fees.Launch Pool Fees: Fee withheld by a V5 or V6 launch hook on each trade in that launch's Uniswap v4 pool - 1% at regime, and up to 95% on buys in the first blocks of an anti-sniper launch's opening window - in whichever currency (launched token or quote asset) the trader paid in.

Revenue.Launch Pool Fees to Protocol: Protocol's share of each fee: 50% by default, 30% on Holder-Rewards launches, 10% during a launch's opening window.

ProtocolRevenue.Launch Pool Fees to Protocol: Protocol's share of each fee: 50% by default, 30% on Holder-Rewards launches, 10% during a launch's opening window.

SupplySideRevenue.Launch Pool Fees to Creators: Creator's share of each fee: 50% by default, 30% on Holder-Rewards launches, 10% during a launch's opening window.
SupplySideRevenue.Launch Pool Fees to Token Holders: Holder-Rewards launches only: the ~40% remainder streamed to the launched token's own holders via the Reward Vault.
SupplySideRevenue.Launch Pool Fees to Token Buyback: Opening-window fees only: the 80% remainder sent to the launch's Treasury Reserve, which bids under the price to buy the launched token back and burn it.

Fees.Referral Fees: Referral payout, paid only on trades with a referrer.
Fees.Community Drop Fees: Community drop share, paid to the launched token's community pool.

SupplySideRevenue.Referral Fees: Referral payout on trades with a referrer.
SupplySideRevenue.Community Drop Fees: Community drop share, paid to the launched token's community pool.

methodology.Fees: Curve mode: flat 1% fee on every bonding-curve buy/sell, read from each trade's own gross USDC amount. methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Curve mode: 50% of the curve trading fee, paid to the token's creator. Post-graduation: 30% of the pool swap fee to the creator, plus the 40% LP share that stays in the pool as reserve growth (the LP position itself is burned at graduation, so this permanently compounds into the pool rather than paying out to a live LP holder).

Fees.Graduated Pool Swap Fees: 1% of the input-side token amount on every swap of a graduated token's WarpDex pool.

SupplySideRevenue.Curve Trading Fees to Creators: 50% of the curve trading fee, paid to the token's creator.
SupplySideRevenue.Graduated Pool Swap Fees to Creators: 30% of the graduated-pool swap fee, paid to the token's creator.
SupplySideRevenue.Graduated Pool Swap Fees to LPs: 40% of the graduated-pool swap fee, retained in the pool as reserve growth (the pool's LP token is burned at graduation).

SupplySideRevenue.Token Taxes To Creators: All tax-token proceeds, paid to the creator's marketing and team wallets.

methodology.Fees: LP fees earned by the listed TickerSpring V7 vaults during the UTC day, including uncollected fees. Measured as the change in cumulative harvested plus pending native-token fees from saved on-chain observations. Excludes principal, stock-price returns, retired vaults and lending.

Fees.Vault Liquidity Fees: Daily change in grossFees plus position.pendingFees, in each underlying token, from the public daily history API. Harvesting moves fees between these counters without counting them twice. Missing observations fail instead of returning zero.

Revenue.Vault Fees To Operations: The operations allocation of earned vault LP fees (10%).
Revenue.Vault Fees To Buyback Reserve: The allocation reserved for future SPRING buybacks and burns (20%), measured when fees accrue rather than when the buyback executes.

ProtocolRevenue.Vault Fees To Operations: The operations allocation of earned vault LP fees (10%).

HoldersRevenue.Vault Fees To Buyback Reserve: The allocation reserved for future SPRING buybacks and burns (20%), measured when fees accrue rather than when the buyback executes.

methodology.Fees: The tax ArgusPad's per-launch hook charges on every buy and sell, the trading fee each launch's pool charges (on Portals 3-7 the 1% pool fee earned by the permanently locked launch position; on Portal 8 a 1% base fee the hook charges in the quote asset in its place), and the extra tax charged on buys in a launch's first seconds. Counted in the asset the fee is charged in, at the moment it is charged, so the protocol's later sale of the launched tokens it was paid is not counted a second time. Fees charged in the launched token itself (Portals 3-7 only; Portal 8 takes every fee in the quote asset) are reported in that token's own units and are priced only if DefiLlama has a price for it; it has none for these tokens today, because a launched token's only market is the pool ArgusPad seeded, and pricing it there overstates by about 40% against what ArgusPad's own sales of them actually realise.
methodology.Revenue: The share of fees reaching the ArgusPad treasury at the rate each launch fixes at creation - 10% of every fee on Portals 3-7 and 30% on Portal 8 - plus the whole of the early-buy snipe tax, which is paid straight to the treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The share of fees reaching the ArgusPad treasury at the rate each launch fixes at creation - 10% of every fee on Portals 3-7 and 30% on Portal 8 - plus the whole of the early-buy snipe tax, which is paid straight to the treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rest of the fees, which leave the protocol divided at the weights each launch fixed at creation: the token creator's share, the dividends paid to holders of that launched token, the share added back into the launch's permanently locked liquidity, the share used to buy and burn the launched token, and on Portal 8 the share used to buy the launched token and lock it permanently.

Fees.Swap Tax: The launch's own buy and sell tax, chosen per launch (1-10%), taken by its hook on each swap: on Portals 3-7 read from that swap's TaxTaken, net of the tax the splitter pays itself when it sells launched tokens through the launch's own pool, which is not paid by any user; on Portal 8 the tax part of QuoteFeeTaken's bucketFee. The hook charges it outside the pool fee, so it is not inside Uniswap's fee reporting for Arc.
Fees.LP Fees: Portals 3-7: the 1% Uniswap v4 pool fee earned by the launch's permanently locked position, read as what the locker forwarded to the splitter, net of the position principal that comes back through the same call. These fees are also inside Uniswap's fee reporting for Arc.
Fees.Token Swap Fees: Portal 8: the 1% base fee the hook adds to every buy and sell and takes in the quote asset. Portal 8 pools are dynamic-fee pools whose pool fee is set to zero on every swap, so this replaces the LP fee and goes to the same split; it is not inside Uniswap's fee reporting for Arc. It is the base's proportional part of QuoteFeeTaken's bucketFee, which prices tax and base as one rate.
Fees.Snipe Tax: An extra, time-decaying tax on buys in the seconds after a launch opens, charged by the same hook and paid directly to the treasury (Portal 8: QuoteFeeTaken's surcharge).

Revenue.Swap Fees to Treasury: treasuryBps of each launch's accrued fee, read from that launch's own splitter or escrow (1000 on every Portal 3-7 launch, 3000 on every Portal 8 launch), plus the whole snipe tax, which the hook pays straight to the treasury without passing through a splitter, plus on Portal 8 any holders' share accrued while no holder was eligible, which the hook also pays straight to the treasury.

ProtocolRevenue.Swap Fees to Treasury: treasuryBps of each launch's accrued fee, read from that launch's own splitter or escrow (1000 on every Portal 3-7 launch, 3000 on every Portal 8 launch), plus the whole snipe tax, which the hook pays straight to the treasury without passing through a splitter, plus on Portal 8 any holders' share accrued while no holder was eligible, which the hook also pays straight to the treasury.

SupplySideRevenue.Creator Fees: The token creator's share, at that launch's configured creatorBps, credited to the creator to claim. Takes the remainder of the supply side, so fees equal revenue plus supply-side revenue exactly.
SupplySideRevenue.Launched Token Holder Dividends: Dividends paid out to holders of the launched token, at that launch's configured dividendBps. These are not ARGUS holders, so they are a supply-side cost rather than holders revenue.
SupplySideRevenue.Fees Compounded Into Locked Liquidity: The share added straight back into the launch's permanently locked position instead of being paid to anyone, at that launch's configured liquidityBps.
SupplySideRevenue.Launched Token Buy and Burn: The share used to buy and burn the launched token, at that launch's configured burnBps. It buys the launched token, not ARGUS, so it is a cost carried by that launch's supply side rather than a protocol buyback or a payment to holders.
SupplySideRevenue.Launched Token Buy and Lock: Portal 8: the share used to buy the launched token and lock it permanently in the line's lock vault, at that launch's configured lockBps. Like the burn it buys the launched token, not ARGUS, so it is supply side.

methodology.Fees: What users pay to cross the bridge. The asset's controller on Arc charges the same rate in both directions - on the way in it mints the fee to the protocol and the rest to the user, on the way out it burns the gross and re-mints the fee - and an optional fast-lane router charges its own cut on top for skipping the queue, on the origin chain when depositing and on Arc when redeeming. Anything charged on Arc is taken in the claim token (bCRCL, bGLD, bUSDT, bBTCB), which is a 1:1 claim on the asset held in custody and is therefore valued as that origin asset; a fast-lane deposit is charged on the origin chain instead, before the asset becomes a claim, so it is taken in the origin token directly. Either way the fee is denominated in the same four origin assets.
methodology.Revenue: All the bridge fees and the fast-lane fees go to the protocol's treasury with nothing paid out of it.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All the bridge fees and the fast-lane fees go to the protocol's treasury with nothing paid out of it.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: None. The bridge has no liquidity providers - claim tokens are backed by custody reserves, not by a pool, so there is no supplier to pay.

Fees.Mint/Redeem Fees: The bridge's own fee, charged by the asset's controller on Arc at the same rate in both directions: read directly from the mint event, and as the gap between gross burned and net released on the redemption event.
Fees.Fast Lane Fees: The fast-lane router's cut, paid only by users who choose to skip the queue: taken from the deposit on the origin chain, in the origin token, and from the claim tokens on Arc when redeeming.

methodology.UserFees: Swap fees paid by traders on every swap.
methodology.Fees: Swap fees paid by traders, taken from each Swap event's swapFeeAmount. The Vault charges the fee on the input token; it is booked on the same leg as the volume. When that leg is the output token (a non-core token sold for a core asset), the fee is converted at the trade's own rate, amountOut * swapFeeAmount / amountIn - no external price is used. The amount is exact; only its denomination changes. Because amountIn includes the fee itself and the trade's average rate is slightly worse than the pool's marginal rate, the converted fee reads low by about the pool's fee rate plus the trade's own price impact - a share of the fee, never of volume, and always in the under-counting direction.
methodology.Revenue: The protocol's share of the swap fee, read per pool from the protocol fee controller.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Same as Revenue - the protocol's share of the swap fee goes to the protocol fee controller.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Zero - no part of the fee is distributed to token holders today.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rest of the swap fee: the part that stays in the pool for liquidity providers, plus the pool creator's share when a pool creator has set one.
methodology.Volume: Value swapped through the Ranges Vault, counted once per trade from the core asset leg when the trade has one, otherwise from the token sold into the pool.

Fees.Token Swap Fees: Swap fees charged by the Vault on every trade (swapFeeAmount). The Vault denominates the fee in the input token; it is booked on the same leg as the volume, converted at the trade's own rate when that leg is the output token.

UserFees.Token Swap Fees: Swap fees paid by traders on every trade.

methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: what the trader paid on each swap.
methodology.Fees: Two things the trader pays. The pool fee on each swap - two of these pools run Ellipse's market-hours hook and charge 1%, 2% or 3% depending on whether the underlying market is open or shut, so for those the rate is read from the swap itself rather than assumed, and the rest are fixed at creation. Plus Ellipse's own 0.5% on swaps routed through its front end, read from the event its fee collector emits when it is emptied, which reports what actually reached the treasury rather than what was sent.
methodology.Revenue: Ellipse's 0.5% interface fee, kept in full. It is charged on every swap routed through its front end, which is a wider set than the pools whose volume is reported here, so it is not 0.5% of that volume and should not be read as a rate on it. It is dated when the collector is emptied rather than when each swap paid it; a keeper does that hourly.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Ellipse's 0.5% interface fee, kept in full. It is charged on every swap routed through its front end, which is a wider set than the pools whose volume is reported here, so it is not 0.5% of that volume and should not be read as a rate on it. It is dated when the collector is emptied rather than when each swap paid it; a keeper does that hourly.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Money going to governance token holders
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The pool fee, which goes to the liquidity providers.
methodology.Volume: Swap volume in Ellipse's own markets on Arc: the Uniswap pools it opened for the assets it bridges (bCRCL, bGLD, bBTCB, bUSDT) and the market for its own token. Each swap is counted once, on whichever side has a price - USDC everywhere except the ELLIPSE market, which is counted on its bCRCL side and valued as the CRCL held in custody behind it. Launchpad launches are not counted: those pools are opened for other people's tokens on Uniswap's shared PoolManager, so their volume belongs to that DEX.

Fees.LI.FI integrator fees: Integrator fee forwarded to Synthra in the FeesForwarded event of each successful LI.FI origin transaction.

UserFees.Relay app fees: Exact paidAppFees reported by Relay for each successful request, deduplicated by requestId.
UserFees.LI.FI integrator fees: Integrator fee forwarded to Synthra in the FeesForwarded event of each successful LI.FI origin transaction.

Revenue.Relay app fees: Relay application fees collected by Synthra.
Revenue.LI.FI integrator fees: LI.FI integrator fees collected by Synthra.

ProtocolRevenue.Relay app fees: Relay application fees collected by the Synthra fee recipient.
ProtocolRevenue.LI.FI integrator fees: LI.FI integrator fees collected by the Synthra fee recipient.

methodology.Fees: The full native-USDC entry price accepted for every BoneYard NFT mint, read from Boneyard's Minted.price event. Excludes BONE genesis reserve, BONE emitted by burns, secondary royalties, and hook swap levies.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: every included amount is paid by a miner in a successful Boneyard mint.
methodology.Revenue: Mint fees less Charge paid to existing Skeletons. Before LP activation, the retained revenue is the project share plus protocol-owned liquidity bootstrap; after LP activation it is the project share plus BONE-buyback funding.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Charge accrued to active Skeleton holders from mint #9 onward (65% under the deployed constant). Charge is measured when it accrues, not when a holder later claims or burns.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The project slice emitted by Hook.ProjectShareAdded plus the pre-LP bootstrap retained by Boneyard to seed its canonical protocol-owned liquidity. If seedLiquidity diverts bootstrap that cannot be paired with BONE into the Hook buyback reserve, that previously booked protocol revenue is reclassified out on BootstrapDivertedToBuyback. Hook-bound revenue is 100% of each of the first eight genesis mints and 35% of later mints.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Native USDC allocated by Hook.BuybackAccrualAdded from post-LP mints for market-buying and burning BONE, plus any pre-LP bootstrap reclassified to that reserve by BootstrapDivertedToBuyback at liquidity seeding. It is counted when funded, not when the owner executes the capped buyback. BONE is the protocol's own value-accrual token.

Fees.Boneyard Mint Fees: The exact price field from each successful Boneyard Minted event.

Revenue.Mint Fees To Project: Project share emitted by the Hook for a successful mint.
Revenue.Mint Fees To Protocol-Owned Liquidity Bo: Pre-LP mint share retained by Boneyard and later committed to its canonical protocol-owned liquidity position.
Revenue.BONE Buyback Reserve: Post-LP mint share credited to the BONE buyback-and-burn reserve.
Revenue.Mint Rounding Remainder Retained In Bone: Native wei left in Boneyard by Solidity's independent integer floors for Charge and the hook share; it is not a project payout or BONE buyback allocation.

SupplySideRevenue.Mint Fees To Skeleton Charge: Charge accrued to Skeletons alive before each post-genesis mint; holder claims and burn-time Charge payouts are settlement of this already-counted accrual.

ProtocolRevenue.Mint Fees To Project: The project portion of hook-bound mint revenue, taken from Hook.ProjectShareAdded.
ProtocolRevenue.Mint Fees To Protocol-Owned Liquidity Bo: Pre-LP mint share retained by Boneyard and later committed to its canonical protocol-owned liquidity position.
ProtocolRevenue.Protocol-Owned Liquidity Bootstrap Recla: Negative protocol-revenue reclassification when seedLiquidity diverts an already-booked bootstrap remainder into the Hook's BONE buyback reserve.
ProtocolRevenue.Mint Rounding Remainder Retained In Bone: Native wei retained by Boneyard from Solidity's independent integer floors for Charge and the hook share.

HoldersRevenue.BONE Buyback Reserve: Post-LP mint funding for BONE market buybacks and burns, read from Hook.BuybackAccrualAdded and excluding seed-time bootstrap diversion.
HoldersRevenue.Protocol-Owned Liquidity Bootstrap Recla: Bootstrap previously classified as protocol-owned liquidity that seedLiquidity explicitly diverts to the BONE buyback-and-burn reserve.

methodology.Volume: Volume is the input amount of every swap, from the Swapped events emitted by the FelynxRouter contracts (v1 and v2). A swap paid in a token without a reliable price is valued by its output when the output is a core asset (WFLR, USDT0, FXRP, sFLR...).
methodology.Fees: Fees are tracked from the fee field in Swapped events, denominated in the input token. A swap is free unless its route beats the best single DEX by at least 0.1%, counted after gas; the fee is then at most 0.5% (0.05% between stablecoins; 0.15% on router v1).
methodology.Revenue: All swap fees go to the Felynx treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All swap fees go to the Felynx treasury.

Fees.Token Swap Fees: Fees are tracked from the fee field in Swapped events, denominated in the input token.

Revenue.Swap fees to protocol: All swap fees go to the Felynx treasury.

ProtocolRevenue.Swap fees to protocol: All swap fees go to the Felynx treasury.

methodology.Fees: Commission paid by limit-order makers (2.5% of converted proceeds and of the LP fees their orders earn) plus the Uniswap v4 LP fees earned by resting order liquidity, booked when an order is settled or partially filled at creation. Amounts in other tokens are valued on the USDG side at the order band's own execution price.
methodology.Revenue: All commission (2.5% of converted proceeds and of the LP fees their orders earn), paid to the TickerSpring treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All commission (2.5% of converted proceeds and of the LP fees their orders earn), paid to the TickerSpring treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: LP fees earned by order liquidity, net of commission, credited to order makers.

Fees.Limit Order Commission: Commission on the proceeds of filled orders, including partial fills at creation (2.5%, snapshotted per order).
Fees.Limit Order LP Fees: Uniswap v4 LP fees earned by resting order liquidity while the pool price moved through its band.

Revenue.Limit Order Commission To Treasury: Commission on order proceeds, paid to the TickerSpring treasury.
Revenue.Limit Order LP Fees To Treasury: Commission on LP fees earned by orders (2.5%), paid to the TickerSpring treasury.

ProtocolRevenue.Limit Order Commission To Treasury: Commission on order proceeds, paid to the TickerSpring treasury.
ProtocolRevenue.Limit Order LP Fees To Treasury: Commission on LP fees earned by orders (2.5%), paid to the TickerSpring treasury.

SupplySideRevenue.Limit Order LP Fees To Order Makers: LP fees earned by orders minus commission, credited to order makers.

methodology.Fees: Everything users pay through Packed: the flat 0.0004 ETH launch fee, the 1% fee on every trade on a Packed bonding curve (Robinhood Chain), the 1% LP fee of every Packed coin's Uniswap v4 pool (after graduation on Robinhood Chain, from launch on Ethereum), the creator tax a coin's creator sets at launch (0-5%, on curve trades and pool swaps), the anti-snipe charges of a coin's first seconds or first block, and the bids paid for seats in packs launched from deposits on Ethereum. All of it is paid by users: launch fees and bids by creators and pack members, the rest by traders. Pool fees are counted when they are collected from the position.
methodology.Revenue: Packed's share: the launch fee in full, 25% of the 1% curve fee, 25% of the 1% pool fee, and half of every seat bid.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Revenue minus the ETH spent buying back $PACKD, which is moved to HoldersRevenue. Negative on days when a buyback spends more than that day's revenue.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The creator's 75% of the 1% curve and pool fees, the whole creator tax and anti-snipe charges, and the launcher's half of seat bids. For a reward coin the creator's share goes to the coin's holders instead.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: ETH Packed spends buying back $PACKD, its own token, on the open market on Robinhood Chain, from the fee wallet and the team wallet; the coins bought are burned. It is part of Revenue, moved out of ProtocolRevenue.

Fees.Launch Fees: Flat 0.0004 ETH paid by the creator for each coin launched.
Fees.Curve Trading Fees: 1% of the quote side of every buy and sell on a Packed bonding curve on Robinhood Chain.
Fees.Token Swap Fees: The 1% LP fee of a Packed coin's Uniswap v4 pool, in both currencies, counted when collectFees takes it out of the position.
Fees.Creator Tax: The creator's own tax (0-5%, fixed at launch) on curve trades and pool swaps, including the decaying anti-snipe tax of a Robinhood curve's first seconds.
Fees.Launch Block Surcharge: The surcharge on buys in an Ethereum coin's launch block, other than the launch's own buys.
Fees.Pack Seat Bids: Bids paid by pack members for their seats in packs launched from deposits on Ethereum.

Revenue.Launch Fees to Protocol: The launch fee, kept in full by Packed.
Revenue.Pack Seat Bids to Protocol: Half of every seat bid, paid to Packed by the factory inside the launch.

ProtocolRevenue.Launch Fees to Protocol: The launch fee, kept in full by Packed.
ProtocolRevenue.Pack Seat Bids to Protocol: Half of every seat bid, paid to Packed by the factory inside the launch.
ProtocolRevenue.Token Buy Back: Same as the HoldersRevenue component, subtracted from protocol revenue.

SupplySideRevenue.Curve Trading Fees to Creators: The creator's 75% of the 1% curve fee (the coin's holders' for a reward coin).
SupplySideRevenue.Token Swap Fees to Creators: The creator's 75% of the 1% pool fee (the coin's holders' for a reward coin).
SupplySideRevenue.Creator Tax: The creator tax and the curve's anti-snipe tax, all of it the creator's (the holders' for a reward coin).
SupplySideRevenue.Launch Block Surcharge: The Ethereum launch-block surcharge, paid to the creator.
SupplySideRevenue.Pack Seat Bids to Launchers: The launcher's half of every seat bid.

HoldersRevenue.Token Buy Back: ETH spent by the fee wallet and the team wallet swapping for $PACKD in the ETH/$PACKD Uniswap v4 pool, on the day of each buy. The coins bought are burned.

Ethereum: USDC trade amount from KyberSwap router Fee events that pay the World by Starra fee wallet in swaps made through the World by Starra app. Solana: USDC platform fees paid to the fee wallet inside Jupiter swaps, divided by the 0.05% fee rate.

methodology.Revenue: All swap fees go to the protocol.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: All swap fees go to the protocol treasury.

UserFees.Trading Fees: 0.05% fee on each swap routed through World by Starra, paid in USDC.
